**1. Observation schedule – 40 observations/month across three shifts** | Shift | Approximate % of nurses (based on current staffing) | Observations per month | |-------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------| | Day | 60 % (≈19/32) | 24 | | Evening | 25 % (≈8/32) | 10 | | Night | 15 % (≈5/32) | 6 | *How we got the numbers* 1. **Determine staffing per shift** – The unit’s roster shows roughly 19 nurses on day, 8 on evening and 5 on night. 2. **Allocate observations proportionally** – - Day: \(40 \times 0.60 = 24\) - Evening: \(40 \times 0.25 = 10\) - Night: \(40 \times 0.15 = 6\) If the exact shift counts change, simply recalculate using the same percentages. **Observation cadence** | Shift | Observations per week | Auditor assignment | |-------|----------------------|--------------------| | Day | 6 (3 × Day‑shift auditor) | Auditor A & B alternate each day | | Evening | 2–3 per week | Auditor A or B (whichever is on shift) | | Night | 1–2 per week | Auditor B (night‑shift specialist) | *Key points* - **Two auditors** cover the unit simultaneously; they rotate so that each auditor observes at least one nurse in every shift over a month. - Observations are scheduled randomly within the shift to avoid predictability and observer bias. - A simple spreadsheet or mobile app (e.g., REDCap, ODK) is used to assign dates/times before the start of each shift. --- **2. What an auditor must record for a valid observation** | Item | Description | Why it matters | |------|-------------|----------------| | **Date & time** | Exact timestamp of the observation | Enables trend analysis and correlation with staffing or supply issues | | **Shift & nurse ID (or role)** | Day/Evening/Night + unique identifier | Allows shift‑level compliance rates and identification of high‑performers or training needs | | **Patient encounter details** | Bed number, procedure type (e.g., wound care, IV insertion) | Contextualizes the observation; some moments are only relevant to certain tasks | | **WHO “Five Moments” checklist** | For each moment:
1. Before patient contact
2. Before aseptic task
3. After body‑fluid exposure risk
4. After patient contact
5. After glove removal | Core compliance data | | **Hand hygiene action recorded** | Yes/No for each moment; product used (soap/water or alcohol‑based rub) | Determines compliance and product availability | | **Reason for non‑compliance** | If hand hygiene was omitted, auditor notes the reason (e.g., “no sink nearby”, “time pressure”) | Drives targeted interventions | | **Environmental factors** | Availability of supplies, time constraints, patient acuity | Helps interpret compliance patterns | | **Observer signature & audit ID** | Auditor’s name and unique audit number | Ensures traceability and data integrity | *Validation checklist (auditor must tick before submission)* 1. All five moments recorded (even if “N/A” for a moment). 2. Product type noted. 3. Reason for non‑compliance documented. 4. Observation timestamp within the scheduled shift window. If any of these are missing, the observation is flagged as **invalid** and must be re‑observed. --- **3. Presenting monthly results to the unit** | Format | Content | Visuals | |--------|---------|---------| | **Executive summary (1–2 pages)** | • Overall compliance rate
• Shift‑level rates
• Top 3 reasons for non‑compliance
• Action items | – | | **Dashboard (PowerPoint slide or PDF)** | • Bar chart: Compliance % by shift
• Line graph: Trend over the last 6 months
• Pie chart: Distribution of reasons for omission | – | | **Detailed report (PDF/Word)** | • Table: Observations per nurse, per shift, per moment
• Heat‑map: Bed‑by‑bed compliance
• Narrative analysis of high‑risk moments | – | | **Unit huddle handout** | • Quick facts: “Day shift 90 % compliance; Night shift 75 %”
• One‑page action plan (e.g., “Place extra alcohol rubs at night stations”) | – | *Key metrics to highlight* - **Overall compliance** = (Total moments performed ÷ Total moments observed) × 100. - **Shift breakdown** – Day, Evening, Night. - **Moment‑specific rates** – e.g., Moment 2 (before aseptic task) often lowest. - **Top non‑compliance drivers** – supply gaps, time pressure, etc. *Action plan template* | Issue | Suggested intervention | Responsible person | Target date | |-------|------------------------|--------------------|-------------| | Low compliance in night shift | Install additional hand‑rub stations at each patient room | Night Shift Lead | 30 Sept | | Frequent “no sink” reason | Re‑layout nursing station to bring sinks closer | Facilities Manager | 15 Oct | | Time pressure during busy periods | Implement “hand‑hygiene pause” prompts on shift start | Nurse Educator | 1 Nov | --- **Bottom line** - **Schedule**: 24 day, 10 evening, 6 night observations per month, rotating auditors. - **Data capture**: Full WHO Five Moments checklist + contextual notes; each observation must be complete to count. - **Reporting**: Executive summary + dashboard + detailed report, with clear metrics and actionable recommendations for the unit leadership.
